title: Smooth morphisms are locally standard smooth
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a smooth morphism of schemes [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] and $x\in X$. Then there are affine open subschemes $V\subseteq S$ and $W\subseteq X$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] with $x\in W$ and $f(W)\subseteq V$ such that, with $R=\mathcal O_S(V)$, $A=\mathcal O_X(W)$ and $\varphi:R\to A$ the ring map induced by $f$ (the composite of $f^\sharp_V:\mathcal O_S(V)\to\mathcal O_X(f^{-1}(V))$ with the restriction $\mathcal O_X(f^{-1}(V))\to\mathcal O_X(W)$), the $R$-algebra $A$ is standard smooth [def-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-algebra].

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 01V7 (label lemma-smooth-locally-standard-smooth, line 7191; proof: 'Follows from the definitions and Algebra, Lemmas 00T7 (lemma-standard-smooth) and 00TA (lemma-smooth-syntomic)'), applied with any affine open V containing f(x); smoothness in the sense of [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] is that of Morphisms Definition 01V5 by more-morphisms.tex Lemma 02H6 (lemma-smooth-formally-smooth)

proof.text:
(Affine opens $V
i f(x)$ and $W'
i x$ with $f(W')\subseteq V$.) Since $S$ and $X$ are schemes [def-pc-scheme], $f(x)$ has an affine open neighbourhood $V\subseteq S$ and $x$ has an affine open neighbourhood $U\subseteq X$; $V$ may be any affine open neighbourhood of $f(x)$, as in the source. The set $O=U\cap f^{-1}(V)$ is open ($f$ is continuous) and contains $x$. Let $B=\mathcal O_X(U)$ and $\mathfrak p_x\subset B$ the prime of $x$ under $U\cong\operatorname{Spec}B$ [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-spec-points], [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. The image of $O$ in $\operatorname{Spec}B$ is open and contains $\mathfrak p_x$, so its complement is $V(I)=\{\mathfrak p\supseteq I\}$ for an ideal $I\subseteq B$ (definition of the Zariski topology) with $I
ot\subseteq\mathfrak p_x$; choose $h\in I$, $h
otin\mathfrak p_x$. Every prime $\mathfrak p$ with $h
otin\mathfrak p$ does not contain $I$, so lies in the image of $O$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime](a) the open $D(h)\subseteq U$ corresponds to $\{\mathfrak p:h
otin\mathfrak p\}$, hence $x\in D(h)\subseteq O$, and by (b) of that lemma $W'=D(h)$ is an affine open of $X$. Thus $x\in W'$ and $f(W')\subseteq V$.

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 01V7 (lemma-smooth-locally-standard-smooth, line 7191): V an affine open neighbourhood of f(x), U affine open with x in U and f(U) in V; affine opens of a scheme form a basis (Schemes, Lemma 01HR region / standard opens of affine schemes, as in Lemma 01I3 lemma-standard-open-affine)

proof.text: ($R\to A'$ is a smooth ring map.) Let $R=\mathcal O_S(V)$, $A'=\mathcal O_X(W')$, and $\varphi':R\to A'$ the ring map induced by $f$ ($f^\sharp_V$ followed by the restriction $\mathcal O_X(f^{-1}(V))\to\mathcal O_X(W')$). Let $j_{W'}:W'\to X$, $j_V:V\to S$ be the inclusions; by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme] there is a unique $f_{W',V}:W'\to V$ with $j_V\circ f_{W',V}=f\circ j_{W'}$, and it is smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes](a) since $f$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Let $\iota_{W'}=j_{W'}\circ\alpha:\operatorname{Spec}A'\to X$ and $\iota_V=j_V\circ\beta:\operatorname{Spec}R\to S$ be the canonical open immersions of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-spec-points] ($\alpha:\operatorname{Spec}A'\to W'$, $\beta:\operatorname{Spec}R\to V$ the isomorphisms inverse to $W'\cong\operatorname{Spec}A'$, $V\cong\operatorname{Spec}R$). By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-induced-ring-map-spec-square], $\iota_V\circ\operatorname{Spec}\varphi'=f\circ\iota_{W'}$, i.e. $j_V\circ(\beta\circ\operatorname{Spec}\varphi')=j_V\circ(f_{W',V}\circ\alpha)$, so $\beta\circ\operatorname{Spec}\varphi'=f_{W',V}\circ\alpha$ by the uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme]. By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes](c) with the isomorphisms $u=\alpha$, $v=\beta$, $\operatorname{Spec}\varphi':\operatorname{Spec}A'\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine] $\varphi'$ is a smooth ring map [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map].

source.place: Morphisms, Definition 01V5 (definition-smooth) and Lemma 01V6 (lemma-smooth-characterize, line 7048), (1) => (2); the definition of [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] is that of 01V5 by More on Morphisms, Lemma 02H6 (lemma-smooth-formally-smooth), carried by lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine

proof.text: (A principal localization of $A'$ at $x$ is standard smooth.) Let $\mathfrak q\subset A'$ be the prime of $x$ under $W'\cong\operatorname{Spec}A'$ [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-spec-points]. By step 2 and [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-locally-standard-smooth] there is $g\in A'$, $g\notin\mathfrak q$, such that $A'_g$ with $R\to A'\to A'_g$ is a standard smooth $R$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-algebra]: there are $n\ge c\ge0$, $f_1,\dots,f_c\in R[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ and an $R$-algebra isomorphism $\gamma:R[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(f_1,\dots,f_c)\to A'_g$ under which $\det(\partial f_j/\partial x_i)_{1\le i,j\le c}$ maps to a unit.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 00TA (lemma-smooth-syntomic, line 37438), cited in the proof of Morphisms Lemma 01V7

proof.text: (The affine open $W=D(g)$.) Let $W=D(g)\subseteq W'$ be the basic open of $g\in\mathcal O_X(W')$ [lem-weil-pbc-basic-open-function]. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime](a) applied to the affine open $W'$, $x\in D(g)$ because $g\notin\mathfrak q$; by (b), $W$ is an affine open of $X$ and the restriction $\rho:A'=\mathcal O_X(W')\to A=\mathcal O_X(W)$ is a localization of $A'$ at $\{1,g,g^2,\dots\}$, so (universal property of localization) there is a unique ring isomorphism $\lambda:A'_g\to A$ with $\lambda(a/1)=\rho(a)$ for $a\in A'$. Moreover $x\in W$ and $f(W)\subseteq f(W')\subseteq V$.

source.place: Schemes, Lemma 01I3 (lemma-standard-open-affine) and Section 01HR (affine schemes: D(g) of Spec A' is Spec A'_g), as used in 'follows from the definitions' in the proof of Morphisms Lemma 01V7

proof.text: (Conclusion.) The ring map $\varphi:R\to A$ of the statement is $f^\sharp_V$ followed by the restriction $\mathcal O_X(f^{-1}(V))\to\mathcal O_X(W)$; since $W\subseteq W'\subseteq f^{-1}(V)$ and restrictions of the presheaf $\mathcal O_X$ compose [def-pc-scheme], this restriction is the restriction to $W'$ followed by $\rho$, so $\varphi=\rho\circ\varphi'$. Hence $\lambda$ is an isomorphism of $R$-algebras from $A'_g$ (via $R\to A'\to A'_g$) to $A$ (via $\varphi$): $\lambda(\varphi'(r)/1)=\rho(\varphi'(r))=\varphi(r)$. Then $\lambda\circ\gamma:R[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(f_1,\dots,f_c)\to A$ is an $R$-algebra isomorphism under which the determinant maps to the image under the ring isomorphism $\lambda$ of a unit of $A'_g$, a unit of $A$; this is a standard smooth presentation of $A$ over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-algebra]. So $V$, $W$ are as required.

lemma Smooth.exists_isStandardSmooth (f : X ⟶ Y) [Smooth f] (x : X) :
    ∃ (U : Y.Opens) (_ : IsAffineOpen U) (V : X.Opens) (_ : IsAffineOpen V) (_ : x ∈ V)
        (e : V ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ U), (f.appLE U V e).hom.IsStandardSmooth
